searched: Read the state air quality notice harvest: 298 notices, 248 saved permit documents and 40 power-like facilities, with each unmatched facility checked by hand.
Read the North Dakota Public Service Commission case harvest of 415 generation cases since 2022 and the documents of every gas case, including PU-24-342, PU-23-325, PU-26-155 and PU-26-284.
Checked every gas or oil entry in North Dakota in the SPP and MISO interconnection queues against GEM.
Checked the EIA monthly generator file for September 2026 and the EIA annual survey for 2025 for every North Dakota gas or oil plant.
Read the news and plans of Basin Electric, Minnkota, Otter Tail, Montana-Dakota, Great River Energy, Xcel Energy and Rainbow Energy Center.
Read every North Dakota row of the possible updates sheet and searched each data center it names.
Answered every data center site the permit harvest found and searched the newer campuses at Harmony Township, Center, Williston and Nekoma.
irp_summary: Montana-Dakota Utilities: the 2024 North Dakota plan adds no named gas plant beyond Heskett 4, which is built, and models Coyote replacement turbines only as a sensitivity case.
Otter Tail Power: the Minnesota plan filed May 15, 2026 proposes a 50 MW gas plant for 2031 or 2032 with no site named, and the next North Dakota plan is due in 2027.
Minnkota Power Cooperative: the 2022 plan page predates the 400 MW Cass County gas plant, which GEM already lists.
Xcel Energy: the North Dakota commitment in case PU-24-342 is the 447 MW Bison plant added in this batch.
Basin Electric and Great River Energy file resource plans in other states, and their North Dakota gas plants are all in GEM.

qa.question: Is the new Xcel Bison plant the same project as GEM's cancelled Xcel Fargo power plant?
qa.finding: GEM lists Xcel Fargo as a 400 MW gas plant near Fargo, cancelled in 2022, with an approximate point. Xcel's filings in case PU-24-342 now name a 447 MW plant at the Bison Substation west of Fargo for 2032, to meet the same settlement duty from 2016.
qa.recommendation: Keep Xcel Fargo as cancelled, add Xcel Bison Generating Station as a new plant, and add a line to the Notes of each plant that links the two.
qa.researcher_notes: Xcel Fargo was last reviewed on October 29, 2026 and marked as no changes. The 2016 settlement required a gas plant of at least 200 MW in eastern North Dakota by the end of 2025. Xcel did not build one. In 2024 Xcel asked to move the deadline, and the commission moved it to the end of 2032 on October 23, 2025. The new site is next to the Bison Substation in Harmony Township, Cass County. The old record has no site beyond Fargo. A new record is cleaner than reviving the cancelled one, because the site, size and timeline have all changed.

verifications.note: Names the 447 MW resource next to the Bison Substation and the 2016 settlement duty.
Order of October 23, 2025 moving the deadline to December 31, 2032.

qa.plant_name: Cerilon gas to liquids complex, Trenton
qa.question: Should GEM track the steam power units at Cerilon's planned gas to liquids plant near Trenton?
qa.finding: The commission approved two gas to liquids plants near Trenton in Williams County, each with a 100 MW steam turbine plant driven by process heat and boilers burning leftover fuel gas. Most of the power is used on site and less than 50 MW per phase goes to the grid.
qa.recommendation: Leave it out of GEM for now. Add each phase as a 100 MW waste heat from natural gas steam turbine unit only if the manual's lead confirms captive waste heat units at a gas to liquids plant are in scope.
qa.researcher_notes: The commission order in case PU-23-325, dated September 27, 2024, approves the site and describes two phases, each with an associated 100 MW steam powered electric facility. Excess process heat drives the steam turbines, and the plant also has fuel gas fired boilers. Output is 65 to 81 MW per phase, depending on catalyst age. All power is sold to Basin Electric and all power used is bought from Lower Yellowstone Rural Electric Cooperative. Phase 1 construction starts in 2026 with operation in 2029. Phase 2 operation is planned for 2033. The application gives the site as Sections 25 and 36, Township 153 North, Range 103 West, about 1.5 miles southwest of Trenton. The state air permit draft for this site, ACP-18233 from November 2024, now returns a not found page and the Wayback Machine was offline when tried on October 29, 2026. The fuel would count as waste heat from natural gas with a steam turbine. Each phase is over 50 MW gross, which is why it is raised here.

verifications.note: Commission order of September 27, 2024 naming two 100 MW steam powered electric facilities.
Site application giving 100 MW gross per phase and the site sections near Trenton.

qa.question: Should the EIP row named Brickhouse Power Plant be matched to Basin's Bison Generation Station?
qa.finding: The Environmental Integrity Project sheet has a North Dakota row named Brickhouse Power Plant, a proposed 1,400 MW combined cycle plant for 2030. It points at GEM ID L100001025913, which is not in the current GEM export.
qa.recommendation: Put L100001047848 and Bison's unit IDs in the GEM ID columns of that EIP sheet row, since it describes Basin's Bison plant.
qa.researcher_notes: Todd Brickhouse is Basin Electric's chief executive, and the row's research note cites a North Dakota Monitor story of May 15, 2024 about Basin's planned gas plant. The size, technology and year match Bison Generation Station, which GEM lists with two 745 MW combined cycle units. The old GEM ID seems to belong to a record that was merged or removed. This is a sheet fix only and needs no change in the database.

monitor.plant_name: Harmony Energy Park data center, Geronimo Power
monitor.monitor_reason: Geronimo Power plans a data center in Harmony Township, Cass County, that may draw on new gas generation, but no gas plant is named yet.
monitor.note: Valley News Live stories from September and October 2026 say Geronimo Power filed for a conditional use permit for the Harmony Energy Park data center near the Bison Substation north of Mapleton. A story of September 30, 2026 says power may come from new renewables, batteries and natural gas, and that the site would use about twice the power of the Harwood data center. The company has a 200 MW solar farm and a planned 200 MW battery in commission case PU-26-284. No gas turbine, engine, size or air permit was found. Cass County was voting on a building moratorium in October 2026.

verifications.note: Names Geronimo and natural gas as a possible power source.
Names the Harmony Energy Park data center and Geronimo.

monitor.plant_name: Polaris Forge 3 data center, Applied Digital, Center
monitor.monitor_reason: Applied Digital's third North Dakota campus near Center will take 430 MW of grid power, and no backup generator fleet has been permitted for it yet.
monitor.note: A Montana-Dakota Utilities release from 2026 says it signed an electric service agreement with Applied Digital for the Polaris Forge 3 campus near Center in Oliver County, needing 430 MW at full build, with first operation in August 2027. In commission case PU-26-155, filed April 23, 2026, Applied Digital says similar diesel engine backup generation would be used at its other North Dakota sites. Its Ellendale site has 252 engines of 3 MW. No air permit or engine count for Center was found among the state air notices read on October 29, 2026. A backup fleet there would very likely pass 50 MW and be an add once permitted.

verifications.note: Names Polaris Forge 3, Center and 430 MW.
Says similar backup generation would be used at other sites in North Dakota.

monitor.plant_name: Project Fighting Pike data center, Critical Data House, Williston
monitor.monitor_reason: A planned data center campus near Williston has no gas plant or backup generator fleet named yet.
monitor.note: KFYR TV reported on March 26, 2025 that Williston city commissioners approved plans for the Fighting Pike data center on the north side of town. Trade reports give seven buildings of 65 MW each, up to 455 MW of load, built in three phases over about ten years. No air permit, gas turbine or engine fleet for this campus was found among the state air notices or commission cases read on October 29, 2026.

verifications.note: Names the Fighting Pike data center approval in Williston.

monitor.plant_name: Coyote Station replacement turbines in Montana-Dakota's 2024 plan
monitor.monitor_reason: Montana-Dakota's 2024 North Dakota resource plan models gas turbines to replace Coyote Station only as a sensitivity case.
monitor.note: Volume IV of Montana-Dakota's 2024 North Dakota resource plan, filed July 12, 2024, tests a case where Coyote Station retires at the end of 2031. In that case it models two large gas turbines of about 429 MW and 393 MW in total, with Montana-Dakota taking a 25 percent share as it does at Coyote. No site, owner group or schedule is described. Montana-Dakota's ten year plan filed in South Dakota in July 2026 lists no new gas plant.

verifications.note: Names the Coyote retirement case and the 429 MW turbine option.
Ten year plan of July 2026 listing the existing 88 MW Heskett turbine and Badger Wind as the only addition.

Supplemental filing by Northern States Power, doing business as Xcel Energy, in North Dakota Public Service Commission case PU-24-342, dated August 5, 2025. It names a 447 MW firm dispatchable resource next to the Xcel Energy Bison Substation in Harmony Township, Cass County, about 10 miles west of Fargo, with service expected in the third quarter of 2032.
Commission order of October 23, 2025 in case PU-24-342. It moves Xcel's deadline for a gas plant of at least 200 MW in eastern North Dakota from the end of 2025 to the end of 2032.
Xcel presentation to the commission from November 2024 in case PU-24-342 that names the 447 MW Bison project.
MISO interconnection queue data. Entry J3163, Northern States Power, Cass County, North Dakota, 481 MW simple cycle combustion turbine, point of interconnection Bison, active, queued July 26, 2022.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. In case PU-24-342 at the North Dakota Public Service Commission, Northern States Power, doing business as Xcel Energy, must build a gas plant of at least 200 MW in eastern North Dakota. Its supplemental filing of August 5, 2025 says it bid 447 MW of firm dispatchable capacity directly adjacent to the Xcel Energy Bison Substation in Harmony Township, Cass County, about 10 miles west of Fargo. The project chart in that filing shows service in the third quarter of 2032. Xcel says it has already spent about 1.6 million dollars on site design, surveys, land options and MISO study payments. The timeline in the filing has the revised plant proposed in 2027, an interconnection agreement and a certificate filing in 2029, construction in 2030 and service late in 2032. The commission order of October 23, 2025 moved the deadline to December 31, 2032. MISO queue entry J3163 is the same project: Northern States Power, Cass County, 481 MW simple cycle combustion turbine, connecting at Bison. The filing gives 447 MW, so that is the capacity used. The status is announced because no certificate application or interconnection agreement exists yet. The point is the Bison Substation, so the location is approximate. The name is chosen to keep it apart from Basin Electric's Bison Generation Station in Williams County. GEM's Xcel Fargo power plant record is a cancelled 400 MW project from an earlier plan. A separate question card covers it.

newplants.researcher_notes: GEM does not list a gas plant at Coal Creek. Rainbow Energy Center owns the Coal Creek coal plant near Underwood in McLean County. Its presentation to a North Dakota legislative committee on September 10, 2025 lists 2+ GW of new natural gas generation at Coal Creek as a growth plan. The same slide set says Rainbow is in exclusive talks with a data center developer on a 2.1 GW power purchase agreement and has 800 acres zoned. A Minot Daily News story of April 15, 2026 says Rainbow is looking to add gas generation and expects 2.1 gigawatts to be available, fed by a new 136 mile, 36 inch pipeline due in 2029. A POWER magazine article from July 2025 says the same plan is under consideration. No buyer has signed, no air permit or commission case was found, and no turbine, unit count or start year is given. The capacity is the 2,000 MW floor the company states. The point is the Coal Creek plant, so the location is approximate. The status is announced on the company's own planning document.
